But before we do that, I'm going to ask, before we rise for a moment of silence, I'm going to ask my colleagues if there's anyone in particular they would like to keep in their thoughts and prayers this morning.

And I'm just going to start by mentioning, unfortunately, the passing of Maya Huber. And Maya was a longtime McLean resident, a civic activist, and former planning commissioner a ways back. She passed away April 11th at Virginia Hospital Center.

She moved to McLean in 1964, was chairman of the Fairfax Federation of Civic Associations, joined the McLean Citizens Association in 1973. Probably the most important contribution of hers is she chaired the Occoquan Basin Student Citizens Task Force, which, of course, led to the 1982 zoning of 83,000 acres in the watershed in western Fairfax County to protect a major source of the county's drinking water.

She strongly advocated and supported legislation in Richmond that enabled the creation of the county's special agricultural and forestal districts in 1983. And in recent years, Maya was robbed of vision and lost her ability to read and drive.

And in her own words, and this is probably good things for all of us to live by, in her own words, she said, quote, Many wonderful friends have since helped me to continue leading my life without a car, and I am truly thankful. It does indeed take an entire village to take care of the elderly, end quote.

And I think that's something we all can think about and reflect on. But if we could keep Maya Huber and her family and all the folks in the Drainsville District who know her and knew her well in our thoughts and prayers, it would be appreciated. And at this time, I'd recognize any of my other colleagues.
